module.title: Quant Programming & Simulation Foundations
module.destination: Use core Python as an auditable mathematical instrument: trace state, branch and loop correctly, decompose functions, choose core containers, enumerate small finite models exactly, preserve rational/float distinctions, manage explicit pseudorandom-generator state, and build reproducible small simulations that are checked against mathematics rather than substituted for it.
module.gate: Page completion is not clearance. Every owned coding capability must be publicly elicited and scored; exact finite mathematics remains the oracle when feasible; simulation must expose model, RNG state/seed and N; independent review is still required.
module.nextBoundary: M09 returns to mathematical analysis. M21 later owns NumPy/pandas/vectorization/plotting, testing/research-engineering discipline and scientific-computing craft; M30 later owns Monte Carlo diagnostics and convergence/error methodology.

sessions.lesson: A program executes statements in order. `stake=12` binds a name to an integer; it is not an algebraic identity that must remain true. Guided check: Trace `x=5; y=x; x=x+2`; does y change when x is rebound?
